state.misconception_label: Confuses the order of operations, believes addition comes before multiplication

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: \[ 3 \times 2+4-5 \] Where do the brackets need to go to make the answer equal \( 13 \) ? I got Does not need brackets because I worked left to right instead of following the order of operations.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It seems like you may be confusing the order of operations. Remember, multiplication should be done before addition. Try solving the expression by first multiplying \( 3 \times 2 \) and then adding \( 4 \) and subtracting \( 5 \). This will help you get the correct answer of \( 6+4-5 = 5 \). Keep practicing and you'll get the hang of it!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that multiplication comes before addition now. So if I do \( 3 \times 2 \) first, I get \( 6 \), and then I add \( 4 \) and subtract \( 5 \) to get \( 5 \). But what if I wanted it to equal \( 13 \)? Where would I put the brackets then?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Great job understanding that multiplication comes before addition! To make the expression equal 13, you would need to put the brackets around the multiplication part. So it would look like this: \( (3 \times 2) + 4 - 5 \). Try solving it that way and see if you get the desired result. Keep up the good work!

score.justification_pass1: The teacher acknowledges the order of operations misconception but provides mathematically incorrect guidance in Turn 3 (the brackets around multiplication don't change the result or make it equal 13), offers no cognitive challenge by simply telling answers, and while the student shows some progress on order of operations, they don't achieve the actual goal of placing brackets to get 13.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides encouragement but fails to scaffold effectively by not breaking down the problem into manageable steps to help the student discover where brackets are needed, and gives an incorrect solution in Turn 3 that doesn't actually produce 13, showing lack of adjustment to student progress.
